title: Reference a Rhino object into a Grasshopper definition
task: Feed a Rhino document object into a Grasshopper definition by reference with connector.Grasshopper.Reference (by object id), so the definition consumes live geometry that tracks the object; Solve and read the parameter back with Get.
script:
# Task: feed a Rhino document object into a Grasshopper definition by reference,
# so the definition consumes live geometry that tracks the object. Address the run
# with a gh_document_id (binds the definition as `ghdoc`).
import Rhino
import scriptcontext as sc
import Grasshopper.Kernel.Parameters as ghp

# 1. Make a Rhino object to feed in (a line on the document).
line = Rhino.Geometry.Line(Rhino.Geometry.Point3d(0, 0, 0), Rhino.Geometry.Point3d(10, 0, 0))
crv_id = sc.doc.Objects.AddLine(line)
sc.doc.Views.Redraw()

# 2. Place a Curve input parameter on the definition and reference the Rhino object
#    into it BY ID. Reference takes one id or a list; it replaces any existing
#    reference and expires the parameter (Solve to recompute).
feed = ghp.Param_Curve(); feed.NickName = "Feed"; feed.CreateAttributes(); ghdoc.AddObject(feed, False)
connector.Grasshopper.Reference("Feed", str(crv_id))
connector.Grasshopper.Solve(True)

# 3. Read it back — one referenced curve, summarised as type + bbox + a handle
#    (the handle is the Rhino object id it tracks).
out = connector.Grasshopper.Get("Feed")
result = "items=%d handle=%s" % (out.Count, out.Items[0].Handle if out.Count else "none")

pitfalls.symptom: The parameter reads empty (Count 0) after Reference.
pitfalls.cause: Reference expires the parameter but does not recompute; and a disabled definition computes no volatile data.
pitfalls.fix: Call connector.Grasshopper.Solve() after Reference, and ensure the definition is enabled.

pitfalls.symptom: Reference raises that the object is not a Curve/Brep/Surface/Mesh/Point.
pitfalls.cause: A typed parameter (Param_Curve) only references geometry of its type; the Rhino object was a different type.
pitfalls.fix: Use a parameter matching the object's type, or the generic Param_Geometry which references any of them.
